items.paraphrase: Where several exits are required, travel to the nearest one is limited to 30 m for occupancies not named in the other cases, including residential, unsprinklered.
items.note: read 2026-11-14 in the official PDF; 45 m if sprinklered throughout (3.4.2.5.(1)(c))

items.paraphrase: Business and personal services floor areas: travel to at least one exit limited to 40 m (45 m if sprinklered throughout).
A barrier-free path of travel needs a clear width of 1000 mm, reducible to 850 mm over at most 600 mm length.
Doorways on a barrier-free path need 850 mm clear width with the door open; same for the route to one bathroom in a residential suite.
A narrow accessible route longer than 12 m must end in a clear floor space of 1700 mm diameter (or 1700 x 1500 mm, or a T shape).
items.note: read 2026-11-14; this is the circle size the code names for route ends; some washroom stalls use 1500 mm

items.paraphrase: Ramps on a barrier-free path need a uniform slope no steeper than 1 in 12 (also 3.4.6.7 for general ramps).
Exit and public stairs: riser between 125 and 180 mm.
Exit and public stairs: run at least 280 mm.
Exit stairs in residential and business occupancies need 1100 mm clear width; 900 mm where the stair serves at most 2 storeys above exit level.
items.note: read 2026-11-14; table text partly garbled in extraction, the 900 mm low-rise case also matches 9.8.2.1.(1)

items.paraphrase: Stairs serving a single dwelling: riser between 125 and 200 mm.
Stairs serving a single dwelling: run between 255 and 355 mm.
Stairs within or serving a single dwelling unit need at least 860 mm width.
Residential living, dining, kitchen and bedroom spaces need ceiling height of 2.1 m over most of the room; corridors and baths have lower area rules.
items.note: read 2026-11-14; table text partly garbled in extraction but 2.1 m is the minimum column; secondary suites 1.95 m

items.clause: Table 4.1.5.3 (NBC 2020 Vol.1 Div.B p.4-9): sleeping and living quarters in apartments, hotels, motels, boarding schools, colleges 1.9 kPa
items.paraphrase: Dwelling and apartment sleeping/living areas are designed for 1.9 kPa uniform live load.
items.note: read 2026-11-14: publications.gc.ca/collections/collection_2022/cnrc-nrc/NR24-28-2020-eng.pdf; text layout scrambled so value-to-row pairing taken from row order and cross-checked against the Ontario Building Code table (also 1.9)

items.clause: Table 4.1.5.3 (p.4-9): office areas on other floors 2.4 kPa; basements and floors with direct ground-level exterior access 4.8 kPa
items.paraphrase: Office floors above ground-level access floors use 2.4 kPa; ground-level and basement office floors use 4.8 kPa.
items.note: read 2026-11-14: publications.gc.ca/collections/collection_2022/cnrc-nrc/NR24-28-2020-eng.pdf; pairing from row order in scrambled extraction; 2.4 applies to upper floors
